heading: Justin Erasmus — Hybrid Music Producer
role: Founder & creator of AlgoRythm Hybrid Music Production (AHMP) and the artist behind Prismatic Wave.

photo.alt: Justin Erasmus in his studio at a laptop, surrounded by holographic 'Algorithmic Hybrid Engine' panels, neon-lit speakers and a pad controller

bio._status: DRAFT written only from facts Justin supplied (2026-10-01). Justin to expand (background, influences, studio) and then set status to 'final'.
paragraphs: Justin Erasmus is a South African hybrid music producer and the founder and creator of AlgoRythm Hybrid Music Production (AHMP). He developed the Hybrid Music Production framework.

Prismatic Wave is his hybrid, AI-assisted artist persona, produced through AHMP. The catalogue counts 11 albums, 5 EPs and 20 singles released in less than 13 months, on Spotify and other platforms, and a wider body of work is shared on Suno.
Justin holds SAMPRA and SAMRO approvals and memberships.

hybrid.title: What is Hybrid Music Production?
hybrid.teaser: Hybrid Music Production combines human creativity and musical direction with technology and AI-assisted music creation, to make commercially usable music and explore new sounds.
paragraphs: Hybrid Music Production is a way of making music where human creativity stays in charge and technology, including AI-assisted music tools, widens what is possible. The producer sets the vision: the concept, the emotion, the genre, the lyrics and the musical direction.

AI-assisted tools are then used to generate and explore ideas quickly: melodies, arrangements, vocal textures and sound palettes that would take far longer to find alone. The producer listens, selects, rejects, rewrites and refines, so every result reflects a human decision.

Finally, traditional production skills turn the strongest ideas into finished records: songwriting, editing, arrangement, mixing, mastering and release. The aim is twofold: commercially usable music for artists, brands and media, and experimental new sounds that neither people nor machines would reach on their own.
